$comment: DRAFT - NOT USED BY THE APP YET. The Story Movie module does not exist; this format is a proposal so content tools can be designed early. Expect changes before the module ships; when it does, the format id becomes "story/1".
title: Little Loops - Story Movie stories (DRAFT, story-draft/1)
description: DRAFT format for the future Story Movie activity of Little Loops (ages 4-7, no reading required). A story is a short animated movie made of scenes. Each scene shows one Coloring background (by id, from data/coloring/backgrounds.json) with up to 3 characters - each a Coloring animal (by id, from data/coloring/animals.json) optionally wearing a Coloring accessory (by id, from data/coloring/accessories.json) - and plays: first the spoken `narration`, then the `timeline` of simple actions one after another (enter, move-to, jump, wave, say, wait). Everything a child must understand is spoken; on-screen text is optional. Proposed location: data/stories/stories.json (one file holding all stories, like the other content files, because a static web host cannot list a folder). COORDINATES: scene 600 x 600, origin top-left, y grows DOWN (same as Coloring backgrounds). A character's (x, y) is where its FEET touch the ground = the bottom-center of its 300 x 300 animal box; `size` scales that box (1 = 300 units tall; the Coloring picture uses 1.2 = 360 units; 0.5-0.7 suits 2-3 characters). The Coloring picture's placement equals {"x": 300, "y": 570, "size": 1.2}. Ground lines: keep y between ~480 and ~580 so characters stand on the background's ground. `node tools/validate.mjs` checks story files against this schema plus cross-references (ids exist, `who` names a character in the scene, enter comes first, characters stay inside the scene). Any JSON file under data/stories/ is checked as this format, so its "schema" must be exactly "story-draft/1".

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema file (e.g. "../../schemas/story.schema.json"). Ignored by the app.

schema.description: Format identifier. Must be exactly "story-draft/1" while this format is a draft.

stories.description: Stories in the order the story picker shows them. Ids must be unique.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit.

spoken.description: One short spoken sentence (text-to-speech), warm and positive, in simple US English words a 4-year-old understands (color, favorite, mom). Max 110 characters (hard limit: speech gets cut off); keep it to 15 words or fewer (the validator warns above 15). No symbols, emoji or markup (< > { } and emoji are errors); never scold.

story.description: One short movie: 1-8 scenes, ideally 3-5, about 30-90 seconds in total, with a simple beginning, a small problem or surprise, and a happy ending. Friendly, never scary; no copyrighted characters; characters can have simple invented names.

id.description: Stable story id (also the save key for 'watched' progress); never rename once published.

title.description: Name for grown-ups and screen readers, e.g. "The Picnic".

say.description: Spoken when the child taps the story's tile, e.g. "A story about a picnic!".

scene.description: One shot: a background, the characters in it, narration spoken when the scene opens, then the timeline. The movie moves to the next scene when the timeline ends.

id.description: Optional scene id (for tooling and debugging).

background.description: Id of a Coloring background (data/coloring/backgrounds.json), e.g. "meadow", "beach", "space", "underwater", "snowy", "farm".

characters.description: 0-3 characters on stage. Character ids must be unique within the scene. Characters with an `enter` action start off-stage; all others are visible from the start.

narration.description: 1-3 short narrator lines spoken in order when the scene opens, before the timeline starts.

timeline.description: Actions played one after another (each waits for the previous one to finish). May be empty for a narration-only scene.

id.description: Handle used by timeline actions (`who`), unique in the scene, e.g. "kit". Reuse the same id for the same character across scenes.

animal.description: Id of a Coloring animal (data/coloring/animals.json), e.g. "cat", "dog", "bunny", "bear", "penguin", "dinosaur".

accessory.description: Optional id of a Coloring accessory it wears or holds (data/coloring/accessories.json), e.g. "party-hat", "crown", "sunglasses", "bow-tie", "balloon", "ice-cream".

x.description: Scene x of the character's feet (center of the bottom of its animal box). Keep the whole box (300 * size wide) inside 0..600.

y.description: Scene y of the character's feet (bottom of its animal box), usually 480-580 so it stands on the ground.

size.description: Scale of the 300 x 300 animal box: 1 = 300 units tall, 0.6 = 180 units; the Coloring picture uses 1.2 (360 units). Use 0.5-0.7 for two or three characters.

facing.description: "right" = as drawn in the Coloring art; "left" = mirrored. move-to and enter turn the character toward where it walks.

action.description: One timeline step, selected by `action`. `who` must be the id of a character in the same scene.

enter = walk in from off-stage to the character's x, y; move-to = walk to a new spot; jump = hop in place; wave = wave the raised paw; say = the character speaks a line (text-to-speech, with a little bounce and a speech-bubble icon); wait = pause.

enterAction.description: The character walks in from off-stage to its (x, y). At most one enter per character per scene, and it must be that character's first action.

from.description: Side it walks in from. Default: the side nearer to its x.

moveAction.description: The character walks (turning to face the way it goes) to a new spot and stays there.

x.description: Target feet x in the scene.

y.description: Target feet y; default: stay on the same ground line.

waveAction.description: Waves hello or goodbye with the raised paw (at the animal's hand anchor).

sayAction.description: The character speaks one line; the timeline continues when speech ends (or after a time-out if speech is unavailable).

text.description: The spoken line, e.g. "Hi, Bo! Do you want to play?".
